records.name: Philadelphia Trail Club
records.summary: A hiking club founded in 1931 that leads hikes most weekends in Philadelphia and nearby counties, from easy walks to strenuous outings. Non-members can join public hikes.
records.what_you_do: Join a led hike, check its difficulty rating, and over time members can train to lead hikes themselves. The club also supports trail maintenance and outdoor education.

schedule.text: Hikes most weekends, less often in July and August. Each hike has a published difficulty level.

cost.text: Club membership is $10 a year. Non-members can attend public hikes after registering as a guest.

first_step.how: Pick a public hike from the hike list and register as a guest through the non-member registration page
first_step.basis: The club says non-members can attend public hikes, and its hikes range from very easy to strenuous, so a newcomer can choose one that fits.

records.notes: Dues of $10 appear on the club site and in the Inquirer (June 2025). The site gives two spellings of the hike chair email, so use the general address. Status is probably active: the site is working and describes current weekend hikes, but shows no dated hike listings. Meeting places are given per hike.

records.name: Philadelphia Canoe Club
records.summary: A paddling club founded in 1905 that teaches canoeing, kayaking and stand-up paddleboarding from its boathouse on Ridge Avenue. It runs trips, training and social paddles through the year.
records.what_you_do: Take instruction, join club paddles and trips, and help with fall work days at the boathouse.

schedule.text: Monthly club meetings plus regular paddles, classes and work days. Listed dates include Oct 10 (fall work day), Oct 19 and Nov 16, 2026 (club meetings).

cost.text: Full membership is a $25 application fee plus annual dues up to $180. Club trips and training are open to the public without membership; trip fees are not listed.

first_step.how: Come to a fall work day or an open event at 4900 Ridge Ave, or email admin@philacanoe.org
first_step.basis: The club trains new paddlers, and its site says trips and training do not require membership.

records.notes: The club site links separate membership pages that were not opened. The Inquirer (June 2025) gives the $25 application fee, up to $180 in dues, and a sponsorship requirement, so check current figures before publishing. The site names no officers and no age rules.

records.name: Feminist Bird Club Philly
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of a national birding group that makes room for women, LGBTQIA+ people and people of color. Members go on bird walks and outings together and share news through a newsletter.
records.what_you_do: Go on guided bird walks, identify birds with others, and sign up for outings through the chapter's link page.

schedule.text: Outings come up through the year, often on Saturday mornings, with sign-up through a form for each walk. The most recent listed outing is a Saturday, Oct 10, 2026 trip to Palmyra Cove in New Jersey.

locations.label: Philadelphia parks, such as Tacony Creek Park, Awbury Arboretum and the Strawberry Mansion Reservoir area

cost.text: Not stated on the chapter pages. Past Awbury Arboretum hikes were listed as free.

first_step.how: Fill in the sign-up form for an outing on the chapter's link page, and sign up for the newsletter
first_step.basis: Outings are open to the public with a sign-up form, but the chapter page does not say what a first walk is like.

records.notes: The Linktree lists 'Saturday, 10/10' with no year. The year 2026 is inferred from the weekday, since Oct 10, 2026 is a Saturday. The national site says the group serves BIPOC, women and LGBTQIA+ people; the chapter does not list BIPOC in community because no exact tag exists. The chapter's email address came from a search summary and was not verified on a page, so it is left out. Chapter status is supported by the Audubon Mid-Atlantic listing and by Billy Penn (May 2025).

records.name: Philly Queer Birders
records.summary: A community group for queer birders in Philadelphia that holds bird outings roughly once a month. Friends, partners and kids are welcome, and it welcomes people who have never birded.
records.what_you_do: Join a birding outing near public transit, bring binoculars or borrow one of the group's extra pairs, and get on the email list for the next walk.

schedule.text: Outings roughly once a month, near public transit. Regular places include FDR Park, The Woodlands and the John Heinz refuge. The newest dated outing on the site is June 2024.

first_step.how: Join the email list, follow the Instagram account, or email the group
first_step.basis: The group says it welcomes all skill levels, including people who have never birded, and it lists how to get on its list.

records.notes: Dormant on the evidence: the newest dated item on the site is a June 2024 outing photo caption. Billy Penn (May 2025) describes outings as several a month, which conflicts with the site's roughly monthly, so the schedule is hedged. Recheck the Instagram before showing this group as current.

records.name: Audubon Mid-Atlantic
records.summary: The Mid-Atlantic office of the National Audubon Society. In Philadelphia it runs the Discovery Center at the Strawberry Mansion Reservoir and leads public bird walks and tours in city parks.
records.what_you_do: Join a public birding walk or tour, use the binoculars the Discovery Center lends, and sign up for event updates.

schedule.text: Public birding tours and walks in Philadelphia parks on weekend mornings, including Philly Birding Weekend tours on Oct 10 and Oct 11, 2026.

locations.label: Discovery Center at Strawberry Mansion Reservoir, plus FDR Park, The Woodlands and East Fairmount Park

first_step.how: Find a walk on the events calendar and sign up through its listing
first_step.basis: Walks are open to the public with a published sign-up, but the page does not say what a first walk is like.

records.notes: The page gives no street address for the Discovery Center, so none is recorded. Several listed tours are in Maryland and are left out. The page does not state whether walks are free. Its contact page is a form, not an email address.

records.name: Adapted Birding (PA Center for Adapted Sports)
records.summary: A birding program for people with disabilities, run by a nonprofit that serves people with disabilities. Guided outings take place on accessible trails across the Philadelphia region, and each walk needs registration.
records.what_you_do: Register for a guided outing, sign the waiver and forms the first time, then walk an accessible trail with a group and look for birds.

schedule.text: Guided outings on weekend mornings through the fall, each with its own sign-up. Listed outings run from Sept 13 to Nov 1, 2026, including Oct 10 at Peace Valley Park and Oct 24 at the Schuylkill Center.

locations.label: Accessible parks in Montgomery, Bucks and Delaware counties

first_step.how: Pick an outing on the program calendar and register through its sign-up form
first_step.basis: Anyone can register for an outing, but space is limited and each person must sign waivers and paperwork before the first walk.

records.notes: The page links an eligibility document that was not opened, so open_to is set to public with registration. Some outings need extra sign-up through partner sites (Peace Valley Nature Center; Birding Partners for the Schuylkill Center walk). The page gives contact through a web form only. Cost is not stated.

records.name: Philadelphia Grotto
records.summary: A caving club founded in 1947 and part of the National Speleological Society. Members care for caves, explore them, teach others and do research.
records.what_you_do: Attend the monthly meeting, learn caving from members, and go on trips with more experienced cavers. The club also guides youth groups on caving trips.

schedule.text: Monthly meetings on the first Thursday of the month. The website does not give the meeting time or place.

first_step.how: Come to a monthly meeting, or read the New Cavers section of the website
first_step.basis: The club holds open monthly meetings and has a section for new cavers, but its site does not say what a first visit involves.

records.notes: Probably active: the site works but shows no dated meetings, trips or news (its only dates are image uploads from 2022 and 2024). The youth page sets rules for youth trips (members at least 14, groups of under 21, up to 10 in a cave, about six expeditions a year); those rules apply to youth groups, not to the public, so they are not published here. Confirm meeting place and time before publishing.

records.name: Outdoor Club of South Jersey
records.notes: Hiking, cycling, paddling and trail-work club based in Oceanville, NJ, with a membership fee. Its home page does not mention Philadelphia, and the Inquirer (June 2025) and a search summary place it in South Jersey. Volunteers work on trails in the Pinelands. Not published as a Philadelphia group.

notes: Searches: 9 of 10 used, budget not exhausted, none left after the last one. Verdicts: publish 7 (Philadelphia Trail Club, Philadelphia Canoe Club, Feminist Bird Club Philly, Philly Queer Birders, Audubon Mid-Atlantic, Adapted Birding (PA Center for Adapted Sports), Philadelphia Grotto), out_of_area 1 (Outdoor Club of South Jersey). Philly Queer Birders is marked dormant because its newest dated item is June 2024. Not recorded as groups: Philadelphia Rock Gyms, Movement Climbing gyms, Go Vertical and Hidden River Outfitters, which are businesses seen only in search summaries. Climbers for Palestine appeared in a search result as an activist meetup and was not recorded. The Valley Forge Audubon Society appeared in a search summary and was not checked, so it is not listed. Blocked: DVOC, the largest birding club named in these sources, needs a manual check. The searches did not turn up a Philadelphia outdoor climbing club or a camping club that is not a gym or a Meetup group.
